sentences.text: Ninjatitan was a massive dinosaur reaching a length of 20 meters.
This extinct titanosaurian sauropod lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Bajada Colorada Formation of Argentina.
The genus contains only one species, Ninjatitan zapatai, known from a partial postcranial skeleton.
Its generic name Ninjatitan honors the nickname of paleontologist Sebastián Apesteguia, while the specific name zapatai recognizes technician Rogelio Zapata.
When first named in 2021, it was considered the oldest known titanosaur, though later research suggested the Russian dinosaur Tengrisaurus might be of comparable age.

While lacking unanimous features to classify it as a somphospondylan, Ninjatitan possesses traits suggesting it belongs within the Titanosauria clade, either as a basal member or within Colossosauria.
Ninjatitan zapatai lived approximately 140 million years ago during the Valanginian stage of the Early Cretaceous in what is now South America.
Its existence spanned between 139.1 and 132.6 million years ago, covering the Berriasian to Valanginian stages.

Researchers suggest Ninjatitan might be a chimera because its anterior caudal vertebra has features like large lateral pneumatic openings and a specific fossa that are found in rebbachisaurids and diplodocoids rather than in somphospondylans.
Conversely, the holotype's dorsal vertebra shows camellate pneumaticity and the scapula has a triangular projection, both features common in titanosauriforms but absent in diplodocoids.

In 2025, researchers Averianov and colleagues concluded that Ninjatitan could not be conclusively assigned to Titanosauria because its anterior caudal vertebrae have large pleurocoels similar to the non-titanosaurian Triunfosaurus, suggesting it should be classified outside this clade.
